subject: ventures/seller-books
auditor: agent session (Claude), independent quality auditor, see run record
professional: a CPA / enrolled agent who prepares Schedule C returns for online resellers; they check first that gross receipts (line 1) include shipping charged and exclude marketplace-collected sales tax and can be reconciled to the 1099-K, that refunds go to line 2 and fee credits net against line 10, that Part III lines 35 + 36 - 41 = 42 ties to what actually left inventory (each unit sold matched to a purchase made before the sale), that line 9 uses the IRS standard mileage rate in force on each trip's date (2024 67 cents, Notice 2024-08; 2025 70 cents, Notice 2025-5), and that re-uploading a report does not double revenue

evidence.correctness: Three outputs recomputed by hand and compared to the shipped code from an auditor-written vitest probe (scratchpad/probe/probe.test.ts importing apps/seller-books/src/worker/services/{books,importers}/*.ts): (1) a 2025 Schedule C worksheet built from seven items, four sales, three charges, meals, supplies and 1,234.5 miles at 70 cents: lines 1/2/3/4/5 = 10500/2000/8500/6200/2300, 8 = 1440, 9 = 86415, 10 = 1040, 24b = 1501, 27a = 3720, 28 = 98116, 29 = -95816, Part III 35/36/40/41/42 = 3500/5000/8500/2300/6200 - all match to the cent; (2) the eBay fixture parsed and run through buildPnl: revenue 125000, fees 20008, postage 875, net 104117, which equals the sum of the report's own Net amount column (3866 + 106272 - 3906) less the label (875) and promoted-listing fee (1240), so the books reconcile to the deposits; refund 4500 = gross 4830 less 330 tax eBay returned; (3) lot allocation 10000 over [manual 4000, -, -] = 4000/3000/3000 and 1000 over 3 = 334/333/333. Mileage 500 mi x 67 cents (2024) = 33500. But a worker probe (auditor's test in a scratch copy of the app, importing the repo's own eBay fixture after creating two SKU-PYREX-2 items at $10 and one SKU-JEANS-1 item acquired 2026-03-01) shows two wrong COGS outputs: the quantity-2 Pyrex order links one item, leaving the second in stock (P&L COGS 1000 for 2 units with ordersWithoutCost 0; Part III line 41 1000, line 42 1700 where 2000 + nothing for the jeans is right), and the 2026-01-05 jeans sale links to an item bought 2026-03-01 (status sold, disposedDate before acquiredDate). Wrong numbers on line 41/42 a user would file, so correctness is capped at 2.
evidence.completeness: ARCHITECTURE.md claims checked by running suites and probes: six importers (eBay, Poshmark, Mercari, Whatnot, Depop, Etsy x2) against fixtures - pnpm test:unit 9 files / 126 tests pass; worker suite (sign-up, import, re-import duplicates, delete import, wrong file explained, viewer 403, lot + SKU auto-link to P&L and worksheet, CSV download, invitations, org cascade, cross-tenant isolation) 7 files / 56 tests pass; re-import of the eBay fixture in the probe: salesCreated 0, duplicatesSkipped 5; lot allocation, sourcing-sheet import, P&L and Schedule C worksheet and CSV all work. Stated gaps, not claimed done: not deployed, billing dark, no e2e suite, fixtures authored rather than real exports (IMPORTERS.md). No TODO stubs in the books services.
evidence.verification: pnpm test:unit: 126 passed (1.4 s); pnpm test:worker: 56 passed (19.4 s). Ten hand-seeded mutants run with quality_mutate.py in a scratch mirror of the app (private repo untouched, git status clean): shipping dropped from line 1, personal-use withdrawal ignored on line 36, disposed-on-Dec-31 boundary, lot leftover-cent rule, eBay refund tax-back, meals at 100%, re-import dedup disabled - all 7 CAUGHT (plus one invalid mutant, desc() not imported, discarded). In the order-to-item auto-link (store.ts) both mutants SURVIVED the full worker suite: oldest-first ordering replaced by title order, and the in_stock filter removed (an already-sold item can be linked to a second sale). The two real bugs found by probe (quantity > 1, item acquired after the sale) are also untested. The Schedule C and importer cores are well tested; the COGS matching path, which decides line 41/42, is not.
evidence.craft: Read src/worker/services/books/{schedule-c,lots,pnl,service}.ts, importers/{store,inventory-store,ebay}.ts, routes/org/reports.ts, client routes/tax.tsx, vitest configs. Pure builders over plain rows, integer cents, every query filtered by orgId, header matching by name, CSV formula neutralisation. Defects: the order-to-item matching is written twice with different rules - inventory-store.ts:126 only links an item bought on or before the sale date, store.ts:156 takes the first in-stock item whatever its date; sale.inventoryItemId is a single column (schema books.ts:60), so a multi-unit order cannot carry its cost; eBay charge rows keep the report's '--' placeholder as orderId (probe output). Otherwise a senior TypeScript reviewer would accept it.
evidence.claims: README: 'v0.1, not deployed', 'Paid plans are built and dark', 'worksheet (not a filing, not tax advice)' - backed (DEPLOY.md, BILLING.md, SCHEDULE_C_DISCLAIMER in every response and the CSV, checked in the worker test). ARCHITECTURE: 're-imports are safe' backed by the probe (0 created, 5 duplicates); 'Lines 35 + 36 - 41 = 42, items written off also count; personal use comes off line 36' backed by recomputation 1; 'Seller Books never computes a fee from a percentage' backed by reference.test.ts; 'Line 9 ... the app does not assume a rate' backed (null rate leaves line 9 blank with a warning); 1099-K federal threshold 'over $20,000 and over 200 transactions' matches the One Big Beautiful Bill Act reinstatement (auditor's knowledge of the IRS FAQ, cited in form-1099k.ts). Importer verification limits are stated honestly (IMPORTERS.md, RESEARCH-2026-11-24.md). One overreach: 'An order is linked to the item it sold ... Schedule C Part III follows the form, at cost with specific identification' reads as complete while a multi-unit order links only one unit. The public front door ventures/reseller-books makes no claim about the paid app.
evidence.fitness: Walked a reseller's year: create a lot, import the eBay report, re-import it, see P&L and the 2026 worksheet and CSV. It produces what a preparer wants for a one-of-a-kind thrift seller. Gaps a preparer hits in the first hour: no 1099-K reconciliation (line 1 vs Form 1099-K box 1a per platform, the IRS's first matching test; the worksheet never shows the gap from sales tax, shipping or refunds); multi-quantity orders understate COGS silently; returned items are not put back in stock (fixture's 'Return accepted' refund leaves the jeans sold); unlinked orders are flagged on the P&L but the worksheet's Part III gives no warning that line 41 is then overstated; line 9 takes one typed rate per year (no rate table, no check that the rate matches the year, no split for a mid-year change), though the free front door's trips.mjs already prices each trip by date from a sourced table. Not deployed, and importer columns are from authored fixtures, not real exports.
evidence.domain: Compared with IRS Schedule C instructions and Pub 334/538 practice: line 1 items + shipping charged with marketplace-facilitator sales tax excluded, refunds on line 2, fee credits netting line 10, promoted listings on line 8, postage and subscriptions itemised under 27a/Part V, 50% meals on 24b, Part III 35 + 36 - 41 = 42 at cost with personal-use withdrawals off line 36 and write-offs flowing into COGS - all standard and correctly computed. Departures: units matched to purchases made after the sale (impossible under specific identification or FIFO), one unit per order, returns not restocked, no line 33 valuation method, no 1099-K tie-out, and mileage priced at one user-typed rate per year rather than the rate in force on each trip's date (2024 67 cents, 2025 70 cents per IRS Notices 2024-08 and 2025-5, auditor's knowledge; the repo's own table records 72.5 cents for 2026 per Notice 2026-10 and a 76-cent rate from 2026-07-01 per Announcement 2026-11, which the auditor could not verify past its June 2026 knowledge). A CPA would sign off on the line mapping, not yet on the inventory matching.

defects.what: Marketplace-import auto-link gives a multi-quantity order one inventory item (free?.shift() once per order; sale.inventoryItemId is a single column), so the other units stay in stock: P&L COGS is understated with no 'without cost' flag, and Schedule C line 41 is overstated and line 42 understated by their cost. Confirmed with the repo's own eBay fixture (Pyrex, quantity 2: one of two $10 items linked, COGS 1000 instead of 2000).

Marketplace-import auto-link does not require the item to have been bought on or before the sale date, so a sale links to a later purchase (probe: 2026-01-05 sale linked to an item acquired 2026-03-01, disposedDate before acquiredDate) and that later purchase's cost moves into the earlier period's COGS. The sourcing-sheet path already has the rule (inventory-store.ts:126); the two copies of the matching logic diverge.

The order-to-item matching path is untested where it matters: replacing oldest-first ordering and removing the in_stock filter both survive the full worker suite, and no test has a quantity > 1 order or a sale before the item's acquired date.

Schedule C worksheet gives no warning when orders in the year have no linked item; their items stay in_stock, so line 41 is overstated and line 42 understated, while only the P&L counts ordersWithoutCost.

Line 9 uses one user-typed cents-per-mile for the whole year with no rate table, no check that the rate belongs to the year and no split for a mid-year change; the repo's free engine (ventures/reseller-books/trips.mjs) already prices each trip by date from a sourced IRS table.

No 1099-K reconciliation: the worksheet never sets line 1 beside each platform's reportable gross (which can include buyer-paid sales tax and shipping), the first thing an IRS matching notice and a preparer compare.
A refund for a returned item ('Return accepted') does not put the item back in stock, so its cost stays in COGS instead of closing inventory; no warning.
ARCHITECTURE says an order is linked to 'the item it sold' and Part III uses specific identification, without stating the one-item-per-order limit.
eBay charge rows store the report's '--' placeholder as orderId (Order number '--' on the promoted-listings fee row) instead of null.

verdict: Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, verification 2; median 3); finished against what it claims (completeness 3). The Schedule C line mapping is what a reseller's preparer would use: a 2025 worksheet worked by hand from the form (gross with shipping, refunds on line 2, fee credits netting line 10, ads on 8, postage and subscriptions in Part V, 50% meals, mileage at 70 cents, Part III 35 + 36 - 41 = 42 with personal use and write-offs) matches to the cent, the eBay importer's books reconcile to the report's own net column, and re-uploads are deduplicated. Tests pass (126 unit, 56 worker) and caught 7 of 9 valid seeded mutants. The cost-of-goods matching on marketplace import is wrong in two common cases, both shown with the app's own eBay fixture: a quantity-2 order costs one unit, and a sale can take an item bought after it; both move Part III line 41/42, and both seeded mutants in that path survived. A preparer would also want a 1099-K tie-out, a per-trip-date mileage rate (the free front door already has one) and returns put back in stock. Not deployed.
